topic: Trigger points: what those tight knots actually are

slides.headline: What are those tight knots, really?
slides.sub: Trigger points explained, without the myths.

slides.title: Myth: knots are tangled muscle
slides.body: Those tender spots aren't balls of tangled muscle or trapped toxins. Researchers still debate exactly what trigger points are, but they're generally described as sensitive areas in a muscle that feel tight and ache.

slides.title: Why they refer pain elsewhere
slides.body: Pressing a spot in your upper shoulder and feeling it up your neck is common. The nervous system shares signals between nearby areas, so where you feel it isn't always where it's coming from.

slides.title: What tends to make them flare
slides.body: Long hours in one position, sudden jumps in training, stress and poor sleep are common contributors. They often show up in the upper shoulders, neck, lower back and around the hips.

slides.title: What massage can and can't do
slides.body: Remedial massage can ease tenderness and help you feel looser for a while. Research suggests the effects are usually short term, so it works well alongside movement, not instead of it.

slides.title: Keep the benefit going
slides.body: After a session, move the area gently, break up long sitting with short walks and build strength gradually. Regular movement tends to keep those spots calmer than waiting for the next massage.

caption:
Those tight knots in your shoulders aren't tangled muscle or trapped toxins.

Trigger points are generally described as sensitive, tender spots in a muscle, and researchers still debate exactly what's going on in them. Pressing one can send an ache somewhere nearby, which is why a spot in your shoulder can feel like it's in your neck. Long hours in one position, training spikes, stress and poor sleep often make them grumpier.

Remedial massage can ease that tenderness and help you feel looser for a while. The effects are usually short term, so keep moving afterwards: gentle movement, short walks between sitting and gradual strength work help keep things calm.
